title: The Rights of Children upon Parents in Tarbiyah

text_simplified: The text discusses the rights of children upon their parents, mentioning Prophetic hadiths that urge raising children upon obedience and birr (righteousness and kindness). It also warns against excessive play or preoccupation with what harms the child. The aim is to guide parents in raising their children with sound tarbiyah (Islamic upbringing).

review_defects.why: The Arabic 'إطالة' means prolonging or extending the duration of play, not necessarily excessive in quantity. The English 'excessive play' shifts the meaning to too much play overall.
The Arabic 'صالحة' means righteous or good, but the English 'sound' implies correct or healthy, losing the moral/righteous connotation of the original.
